questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very interested in finding a uni abroad with good subject options and I knew i wanted to go to australia due to the weather and also the lack of language barriers.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was some of the best months ever, would definitely recommend doing a semester abroad!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, we got loads of emails as well as had an intro day for all the exchange students where we got oriented.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were loads of welcome emails as well as some intro meetings. I was also staying at student accommodation on campus which helped loads with the transition, the staff were so helpful and answered any questions and confusion I had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think staying at the uni accommodation made my transition easy. The staff were helpful and being around other students who were doing the same intro days was very helpful. Other than that the uni itself also helped and had an intro meeting just for the exchange students as well as an entire intro week with tours and fairs to show which clubs the uni has to offer.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I applied very late because originally I wanted to find accommodation on my own but as the time got closer to the moving date I didn't have anywhere, so I started to look at the uni accommodation. There were several options but most were filled up at the time and the only one with space was IH.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were three different meal options at the accommodation; full catered, half meal plan and minimum. The rooms were then allocated according to if you need to get kitchen access based on the chosen meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive, but if you can do it i would. It is much more social than living alone and I met some of the best people during my stay abroad. I talked to some other exchange students who found living off campus a bit lonely and found it difficult to find friends. It also makes the transition of moving across the world easier as the staff is there to help in any way you need. They also did their own intro week parallel to the uni one which allowed me to get to know all the other people I lived with and it was a lot of fun. Great experience overall.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't the easiest thing to do ever and there are a lot of pages to navigate but overall it was fine.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to look through the handbook and choose courses that you want to take and are in the right semester and then register through their portals.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you were unable to register there were student hubs on campus that could help you and then also you could email the student services.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I took four difficult courses all of which were relevant to my studies. If I did it again I would probably have taken one less serious subject so I would have been a bit less stressed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think some of the professors were great but there were some that were not the best and seemed like they didn't want to teach.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level is similar to that of at KU but the exam format is quite different because they were all closed book and some were even non calculator.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At KU I was used to having 2 courses at a time because we do the blok struktur, but at Melbourne it was all four courses at once which took a while to adjust to the juggling of. There was also less focus on the class time and more focus on lectures. They left you to do a lot of the work in your free time. In the beginning I found it difficult because I thought you had to do all the prep work for the tutorials but as the semester went on I realised they didn't require that much prep which took some of the pressure off.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Elements of Quantum Computing, Condensed Matter Physics 3, Theoretical Physics 3, Sub-atomic Physics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Condensed Matter Physics 3 and Theoretical Physics 3 they were challenging but the professors were great and willing to answer any questions you had. I think Elements of Quantum Computing was also a good subject but as it was a second year subject it was not very challenging. Don't take Sub-atomic Physics, the professors were not good at lecturing and it was often difficult to follow their train of thought. In the final exam there were also several mistakes which students noticed and corrected. It seemed like they didn't want to teach.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wasn't planning on living on campus to start with and that ended up being very expensive. And alcohol (other than wine) is so so so expensive, definitely more than what I was expecting.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transport in Melbourne is very expensive like 5 AUD for one ride on the tram, but one could not tap their cards unless there were inspectors to save loads of money. You could also buy a cheap bike to get around. My food was included in the rent so I didn't have to go grocery shopping.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many clubs and societies to be a part of, there was something for everything.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was mostly involved with the sports and social activities arranged through my accommodation, such as intercollegiate sports and culture nights and pub crawls. There was also a plethora of activities at the uni that I didn't really utilise that much because I didn't have that much time next to uni and social stuff at my college.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend trying a bit of everything in the beginning and meeting people through those activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went travelling around to the big cities in some of the weekends. In our mid semester break I went to New Zealand which I would definitely recommend, lots of beautiful nature! After I finished the semester I still had two months before the semester in Denmark started so I traveled around SE Asia which is much cheaper than staying in Australia where everything is so expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there was no language barrier and the people were so friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think going to clubs and societies is a great way to meet local students. The surf club has great parties and two trips during the semester, but the trips are difficult to get a place on. I met all of my close friends through the accommodation, and it was a lot of fun to live so many students together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not many differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the australian football league.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The stress of planning a semester abroad is definitely worth it. I would recommend looking at accommodation a bit early then it maybe will be cheaper

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I met are some great people from all over the world that I can't wait to see again!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The start is always the hardest but once you get through the first few weeks and are more settled it gets a lot more fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
